title: Typing rules
intro: Use an English keyboard layout and type the kana as written.
pronunciationNote: Pronunciation and keyboard input are not always the same.
particlesText: <kana>私は</kana> is pronounced “watashi wa”, but you type <kbd>watashiha</kbd>.
alternativesText: Hints show one valid spelling. If you use another accepted spelling, the remaining hint adjusts as you type.
smallKanaText: For <kana>っ</kana>, usually double the first consonant of the next kana. You can also type it separately.
nTitle: The nasal ん: check what follows
nText: Before most consonants, a single <kbd>n</kbd> works. Before a vowel or y, use <kbd>nn</kbd> or <kbd>n''</kbd> to separate the sounds.
minnaText: The two n characters in <kbd>minna</kbd> belong to <kana>ん</kana> and <kana>な</kana>. Type them continuously.
completionText: A standalone or sentence-final <kana>ん</kana> completes after one <kbd>n</kbd>; a second n is not needed. This is a Pokotype practice rule. In a standard Japanese IME, <kbd>nn</kbd> explicitly enters <kana>ん</kana>.
hyphenText: <kbd>n-n</kbd> is not a spelling of ん. Use <kbd>-</kbd> for the long-vowel mark <kana>ー</kana>.
combinationsText: <kana>しゃ</kana> is a combination. <kbd>shia</kbd> spells <kana>しあ</kana>, so it does not enter <kana>しゃ</kana>.
longVowelText: Type <kbd>-</kbd> for the long-vowel mark <kana>ー</kana>, for example <kana>コーヒー</kana> → <kbd>ko-hi-</kbd>.
punctuationText: Punctuation and whitespace are skipped automatically. No spaces are needed between romaji groups.
errorsText: An incorrect key does not advance your progress. Just type the correct key; no backspace is needed.
timerText: Timing starts with your first correct key. Pressing <kbd>Esc</kbd>, switching tabs, or leaving the window pauses practice.
helpPauseText: Opening this guide pauses practice. After closing it, select “Resume practice” to continue.
